title: Non-blocking follow-ups from frontend-chart-legend-toggle-not-working's PR #391 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #391 (frontend-chart-legend-toggle-not-working), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: No persisted/versioned e2e spec (frontend/tests/e2e/*.spec.ts) exercises the chart legend click-to-toggle feature at all -- not for any of the 11 original toggle targets from frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay (PR #374/#376/#378) nor the 4 added by this task (PR #391). Every verification of this feature across all four PRs has relied on mocked-series vitest assertions plus an ad hoc, non-persisted Playwright MCP/script walkthrough performed fresh each review round -- exactly the gap that let this task's own user-reported 'not working' bug (actually: 4 legend rows with zero toggle affordance at all) go undetected through 3 prior rounds of review each claiming extensive verification. Add at least one `make e2e` spec (likely extending `stock-analysis.spec.ts`) that clicks a representative legend toggle button and asserts a durable, visible change (at minimum `aria-pressed` flipping; ideally also a chart-visible side effect such as a price-line/marker/series disappearing, matching the rigor pr-reviewer's own independent walkthrough used for PR #391) -- so a future regression of this specific feature is caught by the persisted regression suite without requiring a fresh manual/ad hoc browser pass every time.

PR #391's own description states the frontend vitest suite passed '1037/1037'; pr-reviewer independently re-ran `yarn vitest run` twice against the same commit and got 1035/1035 passing both times (coverage percentages matched the PR description exactly, so this isn't a correctness concern -- just a miscounted number in the PR's self-reported test count). Non-blocking, but worth a quick note/correction for anyone cross-checking test counts against this PR later.

Non-blocking, carried forward from the first review round (needs_work pass): the False Breakout effect extracted in PriceChart.tsx (around line 1725, the dedicated effect added to give False Breakout its own click-to-toggle gate) calls `buildZoneRenderData(...)` purely to read `zone.false_breakout` off its returned `.zone` field, discarding the `fillColor`/`lineColor`/`lineStyle` it also computes -- `displayedZones` already carries `false_breakout` directly, so the extra mapping (building unused color/line-style strings on every render of this effect, including every toggle click) is pure waste reintroduced by the extraction. A plain `for (const zone of displayedZones)` would do the same job without it. (Note: the first review round's own notes claimed this had already been filed here alongside the e2e-spec-gap and test-count items above, but it was never actually added to this checklist -- filed now, on the re-review pass that caught the gap.)

Non-blocking, found during the re-review pass that confirmed PR #391's duplicate-accessible-name fix (code-review skill, medium effort): `PriceChart.tsx`'s divergence click-to-explain balloon (`divergenceBalloonAnchor` state, `AnchoredInfoBalloon` around line 2734) is not reset when the new 'Price Divergence' legend toggle turns the divergence overlay off while the balloon is open -- the overlay-removal effect's cleanup (around line 1901) only unsubscribes the click handler and tears down the series/markers, never calls `setDivergenceBalloonAnchor(null)`. Verified this is NOT reachable via an ordinary mouse click or Tab/keyboard interaction in a real browser: MUI `Popover`'s backdrop is `invisible` (CSS-transparent only, confirmed via `node_modules/@mui/material/Backdrop/Backdrop.js` -- `invisible` does not set `pointer-events: none`) so it still captures and closes the popover on any click outside its Paper before that click could reach the toggle underneath, and `Popover`'s `disableEnforceFocus` defaults to `false` so Tab is focus-trapped inside the open popover too. Still worth a defensive `setDivergenceBalloonAnchor(null)` in that effect's cleanup (or folded into the toggle handler) so the invariant doesn't silently rely on `AnchoredInfoBalloon`'s own backdrop/focus-trap configuration never changing.

decisions.decision: Added a new persisted Playwright spec to frontend/tests/e2e/stock-analysis.spec.ts (`clicking a price chart legend toggle hides and re-shows its overlay on the chart`) using Channel (Autoenvelope) as the representative toggle target -- chosen over Support/Resistance Zones, Divergence, Kangaroo Tail, or False Breakout because it's the one overlay guaranteed to render for AAPL's default-range fixture series with no dependency on the fixture data actually producing a qualifying zone/divergence/breakout (gated only on `showOverlaySection && indicatorsQuery.isSuccess`, both already satisfied once `/indicators` resolves). Asserts both the minimum bar (the toggle button's `aria-pressed`/accessible-name flipping Hide<->Show) and the 'ideally also' bar from this task's own checklist wording (a chart-visible side effect): since Lightweight Charts renders the whole pane onto one <canvas> with no DOM node for the overlay line itself, the test diffs a real `canvas.screenshot()` capture taken before vs. after the toggle click (via `expect.poll` to absorb the library's own next-frame redraw latency, not a sleep) rather than comparing against a stored golden-image baseline -- comparing two captures within the same run/browser avoids the font/OS-rendering flakiness a snapshot-matching approach would carry, while still proving pixels on the chart itself actually changed, not just the button's own ARIA state. Also asserts toggling back on restores the original pixels exactly (not just that the button's aria-pressed flips back), confirming the overlay genuinely redraws rather than merely having been torn down. Ran the whole persisted e2e suite (`npx playwright test`) after adding it: 28/28 specs pass, including this new one.
decisions.rationale: Rejected asserting only `aria-pressed` (the checklist's stated minimum) without the canvas-diff addition: this task's own description is explicit that the ad hoc/mocked-series verification this feature has relied on across 4 PRs is 'exactly the gap' that let a real bug (zero toggle affordance on 4 rows) go undetected through 3 review rounds each claiming extensive verification -- an aria-pressed-only e2e assertion would still miss a regression where the click handler flips state but the underlying `useSeriesVisibilityToggle`/`applyOptions({ visible })` wiring silently no-ops (arguably closer to the actual class of bug this task exists to catch than an ARIA-attribute wiring break would be). Rejected Playwright's built-in `toHaveScreenshot()` golden-image snapshot matching in favor of a same-run before/after diff: a golden-image baseline committed to the repo would need per-OS/per-font-rendering tolerance tuning and periodic re-recording as Lightweight Charts/Chromium versions drift, exactly the kind of environment-sensitive flakiness this suite's own existing specs (no screenshot assertions anywhere else in `tests/e2e/`) have avoided so far -- a same-session pixel-equality check needs no baseline at all and only asserts the one thing this test actually needs: that the canvas rendered differently, not that it rendered any particular way.

decisions.decision: Confirmed current frontend test count rather than changing anything: `yarn vitest run --coverage` on this branch (after adding the one new PriceChart.test.tsx regression test below) reports 1037/1037 passing, 98 test files -- consistent with pr-reviewer's own independently-re-run 1036/1036 for PR #391 itself (1036 + 1 new test this task adds = 1037), not with that PR's own self-reported '1037/1037'. No code change was needed or made for this item; it's a documentation/awareness note only, as this checklist item itself says.
decisions.rationale: This checklist item explicitly only asked for 'a quick note/correction for anyone cross-checking test counts against this PR later', not a code change -- recording the current, independently-reproduced count here (rather than only in this entry's prose) is exactly that note, and happens to resolve the discrepancy the item flagged: PR #391's actual count (1036) matches pr-reviewer's own re-run, and today's 1037 is fully explained by this task's own one added test, not a mystery.

decisions.decision: Removed the wasted `buildZoneRenderData(...)` call from PriceChart.tsx's False Breakout effect (previously `for (const { zone } of zoneRenderData) { ... }`, now `for (const zone of displayedZones) { ... }`), and deleted the now-unused `zoneRenderData` local entirely -- `buildZoneRenderData` itself is untouched (still used by the Support/Resistance zone-bands effect above, which is this helper's actual intended caller) and remains covered by that effect's own existing tests. Updated the effect's own doc comment to explain why `displayedZones` is read directly instead. Re-ran the full PriceChart.test.tsx suite (83/83 pass, including every existing False-Breakout-specific test) to confirm the refactor is behavior-preserving, not just a lint-clean change.
decisions.rationale: A plain loop over `displayedZones` (already carrying `zone.false_breakout` directly, per `SupportResistanceZone`'s own shape) does the identical job without computing `fillColor`/`lineColor`/`lineStyle` strings this effect never reads, exactly as this checklist item itself proposed -- no alternative approach was considered since the fix is a direct, narrow deletion with an existing test suite already covering the behavior it must preserve.

decisions.decision: Added a defensive `setDivergenceBalloonAnchor(null)` to the divergence-overlay effect's own cleanup (PriceChart.tsx, alongside the existing `chart.unsubscribeClick`/`chart.removeSeries`/`divergenceMarkersPlugin.detach()` calls), unconditionally -- it runs on every re-run of this effect (a 'Price Divergence' legend toggle-off, but also an ordinary data/theme-driven re-render that tears down and rebuilds the overlay fresh), not only when the toggle is the specific cause. Added a new PriceChart.test.tsx regression test ('closes the divergence balloon when the Divergence legend toggle hides the overlay while it is open') that opens the balloon via a direct `handleClick` invocation (the same mechanism the file's own existing balloon-opening tests already use) and then clicks the legend toggle via `screen.getByRole('button', { name: ..., hidden: true })` -- the `hidden: true` query option is necessary and itself documents the underlying finding: MUI's open `Popover` marks the rest of the page `aria-hidden` while open, which is the actual mechanism (confirmed live in this test: an accessibility-tree-respecting query genuinely cannot find the toggle button at all while the balloon is open) that keeps an ordinary user from ever reaching this toggle while the balloon is open, consistent with pr-reviewer's own finding that this gap is not reachable via ordinary mouse/keyboard interaction today. Mutation-tested the fix: reverted the `setDivergenceBalloonAnchor(null)` line, confirmed the new test fails (the balloon's own `aria-label="Divergence details"` element is still found in the DOM), then restored the fix and confirmed the test passes again. Full PriceChart.test.tsx suite: 83/83 pass.
decisions.rationale: Chose an unconditional reset in the shared cleanup (not a toggle-specific branch keyed off `divergenceVisible`) because the invariant this item asks for -- 'the balloon can never outlive the overlay it explains' -- holds just as well, and is simpler to reason about, when applied to every teardown of this effect rather than special-cased to only the toggle-driven one; a data/theme-driven rebuild tearing down and recreating the overlay out from under an open balloon is exactly the same kind of staleness this item is guarding against, just via a different trigger. Chose to drive the test through the click handler + a `hidden: true` role query (bypassing the accessibility-tree visibility MUI's `Popover` itself imposes) over wrapping the whole interaction in an `act()` block or using `fireEvent` directly on a DOM node found via `container.querySelector` -- `hidden: true` is the standard Testing Library escape hatch for exactly this situation (an element that's present and clickable in the DOM but intentionally excluded from the accessibility tree by an ancestor's `aria-hidden`), and keeps the test readable as 'click this specific toggle button' rather than a raw DOM query that would obscure which element is being interacted with.
